checks.fidelity: def:continuous_map_ordinary_locus (l.838) follows DEC-40. ordY = {y | ∃ U open, y ∈ U, (p⁻¹U).Nonempty, IsEvenlyCoveredSet p U}. IsEvenlyCoveredSet says each component connectedComponentIn (p⁻¹U) x is homeomorphic to U by a map that agrees with p, which is the paper's literal 'maps each connected component of p⁻¹(U) homeomorphically onto U'. ordX = p⁻¹(ordY). Nothing trivialises the notion: ordY ⊆ range p is proved, and nFold (-2 and 1 ordinary, the fold value -1 not) and unitTrue give non-trivial witnesses. rem:ordinary_locii_open_but (l.843): both loci are open; ordX needs continuity, which the definition assumes. Over a LocallyConnectedSpace source the restriction ord(X) → ord(Y) is always a surjective covering map. That hypothesis is weaker than the §3 standing local path-connectedness, as DEC-39 and kb/0007 allow. 'May not be connected' is witnessed on both sides: nFold for ord(Y); |·| and nFold for ord(X). I re-derived nFold by hand: x on (-∞,0], -x on [0,1], x-2 on [1,∞). rem:singular_on_singular is proved without continuity. lem:spread_partial_covering (l.851) carries continuity of p, IsPortly X₁, Y₁ open, MapsTo p X₁ Y₁, and IsCoveringMap ∧ Surjective of the restriction (DEC-40). Its extra instances are T2Space X and LocallyConnectedSpace X. Both are standing assumptions, both appear in the paper's own definition of portly (l.364: 'X Hausdorff locally connected'), and the proof uses both (the disjoint W, W' and 'a connected open V ∋ x'). Surjectivity is shown necessary for Y₁ ⊆ ord(Y) (unitTrue), and the non-surjective form spread_partial_covering' is proved. cex:openess (l.870) holds as written up to ℝ ≅ ℝ×{0} (minor 1 below): p is continuous and a spread, X → p(X) is a homeomorphism and so a surjective covering map, and ord(Y) = ∅. cex:portlyness item 1 (l.875): non-injectivity needs only that the restriction is an open map and Y₁ is open; x ∉ ord(X) and p(x) ∉ ord(Y) use LocallyConnectedSpace X. The cheap inhabitant Prod.fst on ℝ×{0} is present. Item 2 (l.877): portlyX is the paper's set (|x| ≥ 1 together with λx for λ ∈ (0,1], ‖x‖ = 1, x ∈ ℚ²) and portlyInv is the paper's p. portlyTop = generateFrom(subspace components of X ∩ U). isSpread_portlyι is a genuine fixed point, with components taken in portlyTop itself. le_portlyTop_of_isSpread proves every τ making Subtype.val a spread satisfies τ ≤ portlyTop, i.e. is finer. I checked this argument: a τ-component is subspace-preconnected, so it lies inside a subspace component, which is therefore τ-open. Hence 'the coarsest topology making the injection a spread' exists and is portlyTop, and this is the paper's space, not a reading. cex_portlyness_paper proves, on that topology, every property the paper lists: T2, second countable, locally path-connected, the inner rays ≃ₜ Σ ℕ, Ioo 0 1, p a spread, X₁ = Y₁ open, X₁ IsLocallyConnectedIn, X₁ → Y₁ a homeomorphism hence a surjective covering. It also proves ord(Y) = ord(X) = ∅, ¬Dense X₁, and that all three conclusions of the lemma fail. Since T2Space and LocallyConnectedSpace hold, it refutes the density-free Lean lemma exactly. The ord(Y) = ∅ mechanism is sound: an open subset of U inside ratSlope is empty. lem:ord_iso is at least as strong as the paper's. No hypothesis is vacuous, circular or unsatisfiable. DEC-40 is applied in the definition, the remark, the lemma and both counterexamples. DEC-39, DEC-41 and DEC-42 do not bear on l.822-902.

issues.problem: The paper's X is ℝ × {0} with p the inclusion into ℝ². The Lean uses X = ℝ with p = x ↦ (x, 0), and Y = ℝ × ℝ rather than EuclideanSpace. These are homeomorphic copies, and the claims transfer by image_ordY_of_homeomorph, so nothing is weakened. The object is not literally the paper's, and the docstring does not say so. This repeats AUDIT-2's minor.

questions_for_master: rem:ordinary_locii_open_but is closed and marked. Under DEC-40 ('covering' = surjective covering map), the natural sufficiency reading of 'the only obstruction is the connectedness of ord(X)' (connected ⇒ covering) is proved in an unconditional, stronger form. The necessity reading is false, and abs_ordX_not_isPreconnected_covering refutes it. That reading is disclosed as a finding and as a question to the author. If the master treats the phrase as a reading in the campaign's sense ('partial — … or a reading'), the row becomes partial and the docstring mark must drop. Both readings are formalized, so only the status label is at stake.
